reason: Both conversations asked the right first question (what the smell is like) and both correctly told her to unplug and stop using the appliance once the hot-plastic smell, warm plug and buzzing came out. Conversation 2 went further on everything that matters next: it gave 999/fuse-box instructions if smoke or flames appear, told her how to protect her food, warned her not to open the back panel, and crucially pointed her to check the make/model against the Electrical Safety First recall checker and manufacturer, which lines up directly with the hidden Beko fire-risk safety notice, and noted replacement is reasonable for an old unit. Conversation 1 never asked for make, model or age and never mentioned a recall, so the homeowner would be left with a generic 'get an engineer' instruction and no route to the free manufacturer remedy. Conversation 2's first reply was overlong and suggested pulling the fridge out before the smell type was known, but that is a minor flaw against its much more complete and correct escalation.
